newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Three more die in Russian nuclear warship accident.
newsitem.headline: Three more die in Russian nuclear warship accident.

text.p: Three people died on Tuesday from injuries received in an accident during engine tests on a new Russian nuclear-powered warship, taking the death total to four, Interfax news agency said.
The agency said one man had died of burns last Friday, when a steam pipe in the subsidiary mechanism on the Pyotr Veliky ruptured in the Baltic port of Kaliningrad.
Two others were still in a serious condition with severe burns.
A navy spokesman said on Monday the pipe was not linked to the reactor and that radiation levels were not affected.
Construction of the cruiser began a decade ago, but the navy is still waiting for money to finish it.

The accident followed renewed concern about the security of Russia's nuclear arsenal raised in a leaked U.S. intelligence report, which said chaotic political and economic reforms and a resultant cash crisis had led to a weakening of control.
Russian officials denied any lapses in security.
The Pyotr Veliky, due to enter service this year, was involved in an unrelated accident earlier this month when a Swedish jet crashed into the Baltic Sea just metres from it, killing the pilot.

Russian naval officials accused the Swedes of carrying out a dummy attack on the vessel. Swedish officials denied the charge, saying the pilot was trying to aviod a Russian submarine reconnaissance airplane in the vicinity.
